name: The Narmer Palette
under: Predynastic Egypt < Ancient Egypt < Nile Valley & Northeast Africa < Africa
summary: A carved schist palette showing a king smiting an enemy, and probably the most over-read object in Egyptology.

name: The Speed of Egyptian State Formation
under: Predynastic Egypt < Ancient Egypt < Nile Valley & Northeast Africa < Africa
summary: Egypt went from pre-state to unified state in six or seven centuries, where the same journey in Southwest Asia took four or five millennia.

name: Amazigh
summary: Indigenous peoples of North Africa, continuous through Punic, Roman, Arab and French rule.

name: Bantu-Speaking Peoples
summary: Their expansion carried farming, ironworking and a language family across a third of a continent.

name: Cattle Herding in Africa
summary: The oldest uncontroversial domestic cattle in Africa, in Egypt's Western Desert -- introduced from the Near East rather than domesticated locally.

name: African Cereal Domestication
summary: Pearl millet in the West African Sahel and sorghum in eastern Sudan: two independent African domestications of indigenous cereals.

name: Thule
summary: Ancestors of the Inuit, who crossed the American Arctic in a few centuries with dog sleds and toggling harpoons.

name: North American Megafaunal Extinction
summary: At least 37 genera, some four-fifths of North America's large mammals, disappear near the end of the Pleistocene.

name: Huns
summary: Arrived on the Danube within a generation and broke the Roman order in the west without ever holding a city.

name: Sarmatians
summary: Successors to the Scythians on the western steppe, and heavy cavalry the Romans learned from.

name: Turkic Peoples
summary: Spread from Mongolia to Anatolia over a millennium, founding states from the Gokturks to the Ottomans.

name: Xiongnu
summary: Steppe confederation whose pressure shaped Han policy, the frontier walls, and the westward movement of peoples.

name: Scythians
under: Eurasian Steppe < Central Asia & the Steppe

name: The Yayoi Redating Controversy
summary: In 2003 a national museum used AMS dating to move the start of the Yayoi back five centuries, and the field has still not settled where it lands.

name: Battle of Actium
under: Late Republic < Roman Republic < Ancient Rome < Mediterranean < Europe
summary: Octavian's naval victory over Antony and Cleopatra; effective end of the Republic.

name: Assassination of Julius Caesar
under: Late Republic < Roman Republic < Ancient Rome < Mediterranean < Europe
summary: Caesar assassinated on the Ides of March, 44 BCE, by a conspiracy of senators.

name: Celtic Peoples
summary: A shared language, art and metalwork across Iron Age Europe, never a single state.

name: Germanic Peoples
summary: Named as an outside threat by Rome and eventually the founders of its successor kingdoms.

name: Sami
summary: Reindeer-herding people of Fennoscandia, and among the few European peoples never to form a state.

name: Slavic Peoples
summary: Expanded across eastern and southeastern Europe in the centuries after Rome, with little written trace of the process.

name: The 8.2 Kiloyear Event
summary: An abrupt cooling that hit Mesolithic Europe unevenly — collapse in Scotland, apparent resilience in Belgium, and growth on the Atlantic coast.

name: The Steppe Ancestry Influx
summary: A second large population movement, out of the Pontic-Caspian steppe, which reshaped northern Europe and is widely tied to the arrival of Indo-European languages.

name: Storegga Slide Tsunami
summary: One of the largest known Holocene tsunamis, generated by a submarine landslide off Norway and striking what remained of Doggerland.

name: Thirty Years' War
summary: Devastating pan-European religious and political war ending with the Peace of Westphalia.

name: The Acts of Union
summary: England and Scotland became one state, which is the point at which an English empire can properly be called British.

name: Battle of Austerlitz
under: Napoleonic Era < France (Medieval to Modern) < Western Europe < Europe
summary: Napoleon's masterpiece; defeat of the Third Coalition (Austria and Russia).

name: Battle of Trafalgar
under: Napoleonic Era < France (Medieval to Modern) < Western Europe < Europe
summary: Nelson's decisive naval victory over the Franco-Spanish fleet; secured British naval supremacy for a century.

name: Battle of Waterloo
under: Napoleonic Era < France (Medieval to Modern) < Western Europe < Europe
summary: Napoleon's final defeat at the hands of Wellington and Blücher; end of the Napoleonic era.

name: Late Bronze Age Collapse
summary: Systemic collapse of Mediterranean and Near Eastern civilizations c. 1200 BCE.

name: COVID-19 Pandemic
summary: Global pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2; declared over as an emergency by the WHO in May 2023.

name: Global Financial Crisis
summary: Worldwide financial crisis triggered by the US subprime mortgage collapse; deepest downturn since the Great Depression.

name: September 11 Attacks
summary: Coordinated al-Qaeda attacks on the United States; triggered the War on Terror.

name: Akkadian
summary: The first Semitic language written down, and the diplomatic language of the Bronze Age Near East.

name: Ancient Greek
summary: Written first in Linear B, then in the alphabet that carried Homer, tragedy and Greek philosophy.

name: Arabic
summary: Spread with Islam from a peninsular vernacular to the liturgical and literary language of much of Afro-Eurasia.

name: Aramaic
summary: Administrative language of the Achaemenid Empire and still spoken by small communities today.

name: Avestan
summary: Language of the Zoroastrian liturgy, preserved orally for centuries before it was written.

name: Classical Maya
summary: The only pre-Columbian American writing system fully deciphered, recording dynastic history in its own words.

name: Egyptian
summary: Attested across four thousand years, from hieroglyphs to Coptic, the longest documented history of any language.

name: Elamite
summary: Written beside Sumerian and Akkadian for two millennia and, like Sumerian, without known relatives.

name: Etruscan
summary: Non-Indo-European language of pre-Roman Italy, readable in script but still largely not understood.

name: Hebrew
summary: Ceased to be a vernacular for roughly seventeen centuries and was revived as one, which almost no other language has managed.

name: Hittite
summary: The earliest attested Indo-European language, and its decipherment reshaped the whole reconstruction.

name: Latin
summary: Ancestor of the Romance languages and the learned language of western Europe long after it stopped being anyone's first.

name: Nahuatl
summary: Language of the Aztec state, and the source of chocolate, tomato, avocado and coyote.

name: Old Chinese
summary: The language of the oracle bones and the Confucian classics, reconstructed partly from rhymes in early poetry.

name: Proto-Afroasiatic
summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Semitic, Egyptian, Berber, Chadic and Cushitic; among the deepest families with a serious reconstruction.

name: Proto-Austronesian
summary: Ancestor of a family that spread from Taiwan across the Pacific to Madagascar, the widest pre-modern dispersal of any.

name: Proto-Bantu
summary: Ancestor of some five hundred languages across sub-Saharan Africa, spread by the Bantu expansion.

name: Proto-Dravidian
summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam; possibly the language family of the Indus cities.

name: Proto-Indo-European
summary: Reconstructed ancestor of most languages of Europe and much of South Asia; its homeland is still argued.

name: Proto-Indo-Iranian
summary: The branch that carried Indo-European speech into Iran and South Asia.

name: Proto-Japonic
summary: Ancestor of Japanese and the Ryukyuan languages, probably carried to the islands with wet-rice farming.

name: Proto-Koreanic
summary: Ancestor of Korean, whose relationship to Japonic remains one of the open questions of Asian linguistics.

name: Proto-Semitic
summary: Ancestor of Akkadian, Hebrew, Aramaic and Arabic, reconstructed largely from their shared triconsonantal roots.

name: Proto-Sino-Tibetan
summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Chinese, Tibetan and Burmese; its internal structure is much less settled than Indo-European's.

name: Proto-Uralic
summary: Reconstructed ancestor of Finnish, Hungarian, Estonian and the Samoyedic languages of Siberia.

name: Quechua
summary: Spread as the administrative language of the Inca state and still spoken by millions across the Andes.

name: Sanskrit
summary: Language of the Vedas, and the grammar Panini wrote for it is still the most complete description of any ancient language.

name: Sumerian
summary: The first written language, and an isolate: no relative has ever been established for it.

name: Black Death
summary: Bubonic plague pandemic that killed 30–60% of Europe's population and swept Asia and North Africa.

name: Alphabetic Writing
summary: One sign per sound rather than per syllable or word, which made literacy learnable in weeks.

name: Antibiotics
summary: Fleming's penicillin; bacterial infection stopped being a common cause of death.

name: Practical Electric Lighting
summary: Decoupled the working day from daylight.

name: The Human Genome Sequenced
summary: A species reading its own instructions.

name: Germ Theory of Disease
summary: Established that specific microbes cause specific diseases, which made surgery survivable.

name: Gunpowder
summary: A Chinese alchemical accident that ended the military logic of the walled city.

name: The Integrated Circuit
summary: Many components on one wafer, which is why computing kept getting cheaper.

name: Iron Smelting
summary: Hittite-era bloomery iron; the metal that made tools cheap rather than precious.

name: Magnetic Compass
summary: Made open-water navigation repeatable rather than lucky.

name: Movable Type
summary: Bi Sheng's ceramic type; reusable characters four centuries before Gutenberg.

name: Controlled Nuclear Fission
summary: The first self-sustaining chain reaction, under a squash court in Chicago.

name: Packet-Switched Networking
summary: The first ARPANET link; messages broken into pieces that route themselves.

name: Papermaking
summary: Cheap writing material from plant fibre, in China centuries before it reached the west.

name: Powered Flight
summary: Twelve seconds at Kitty Hawk.

name: The Printing Press
summary: Movable metal type and a screw press in Mainz; the first information technology with a mass market.

name: The Steam Engine
summary: Newcomen's atmospheric engine; work no longer limited by muscle, wind or falling water.

name: The Telescope
summary: Turned the sky into something to be examined rather than contemplated.

name: The Transistor
summary: The switch that made computing small, cheap and eventually universal.

name: Vaccination
summary: Jenner's cowpox inoculation, and the beginning of deliberate control of infectious disease.

name: Woodblock Printing
summary: Text carved and reproduced in quantity in Tang China, long before movable type.

name: Zero as a Number
summary: Brahmagupta gave rules for arithmetic with zero and with negatives, not merely a placeholder.

name: Berlin Conference
under: Scramble for Africa < Multi-Regional Empires < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: European powers agreed rules for the partition of Africa; no African representatives present.

name: Columbus reaches the Americas
summary: Christopher Columbus's first landfall in the Bahamas; opened sustained contact between the Old World and the Americas.

name: The Amber Road
summary: Baltic amber reaching the Mediterranean, and evidence of long-distance exchange well before any empire organised it.

name: The Atlantic Slave Trade
summary: Some twelve million people shipped from Africa to the Americas, and the demographic and economic foundation of the Atlantic world.

name: The Hanseatic League
summary: A league of merchant towns that ran the northern European economy without being a state.

name: Indian Ocean Trade
summary: Monsoon-driven and older than the Silk Road, carrying more goods by volume than any overland route.

name: The Manila Galleon Trade
summary: Silver from Mexico for Chinese silk and porcelain, and the first sustained commercial link across the Pacific.

name: The Silk Road
summary: Not one road but a relay of routes moving silk, horses, faith and plague between China, India, Persia and Rome.

name: Trans-Saharan Trade
summary: Gold north, salt south, and the wealth that built Mali, Songhai and the libraries of Timbuktu.

name: Artificial Mummification
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Deliberate preparation of the dead, practised on the Atacama coast two thousand years before anyone in Egypt attempted it.

name: Butchery of Animals
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Cutting meat from bone with stone tools, which opened a food source that had been out of reach.

name: Cereal Domestication
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Einkorn and emmer wheat at Cayonu and Cafer Hoyuk: the beginning of the crop package that spread across three continents.

name: Domestic Chicken
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: The world's most numerous bird was domesticated in mainland Southeast Asia, far later and further east than long assumed.

name: Controlled Use of Fire
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Keeping and using fire on purpose, which changed diet, safety and how far north people could live.

name: Cooking of Food
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Applying controlled heat to food, evidenced by fish teeth heated to a temperature that implies cooking rather than burning.

name: Cut-Marked Bone
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Bones from Dikika, Ethiopia bearing marks read as stone-tool butchery, roughly 800,000 years before the oldest known stone tools.

name: Deliberate Burial
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Placing the dead somewhere on purpose rather than leaving them where they fell.

name: Domestic Dog
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: The first domesticated animal, and the only one domesticated by hunter-gatherers rather than farmers.

name: Fermented Drink
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Residues of fermented wheat and barley in stone mortars at Raqefet Cave, made by Natufian foragers from wild cereals.

name: Figurative Art
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Pictures of recognisable things — animals and people — rather than patterns.

name: Horse Domestication
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: The ancestry of every modern domestic horse traces to the lower Volga-Don steppe, not to the older Botai husbandry once assumed to be its origin.

name: Irrigation
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Canals and ditches at Choga Mami in Mesopotamia, the first farming that reshaped the land to suit itself.

name: Use of Pigment
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Collecting and working coloured earth, the earliest hint of decoration or marking.

name: Pottery
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Ceramic vessels from Xianrendong Cave, Jiangxi — made by hunter-gatherers ten thousand years before anyone in the region farmed.

name: Intentional Seafaring
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Crossing open water on purpose, out of sight of the far shore, which requires planning and a built craft.

name: Personal Ornaments
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Shells pierced and strung to be worn, which means signalling something about yourself to other people.

name: Spun Fibre
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Wild flax from Dzudzuana Cave, Georgia, twisted into cordage and dyed turquoise, pink and black.

name: Stone Knapping
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: The first deliberate shaping of stone into tools — the behaviour this app uses to mark where human prehistory begins.

name: Abstract Engraving
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Deliberate cross-hatched patterns cut into ochre — marks that mean something without depicting anything.

name: The Wheel
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Wheeled wagons appear in Mesopotamia and central Europe at nearly the same moment, and which came first is unresolved.

name: Structural Use of Wood
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Two interlocking notched logs from Kalambo Falls, Zambia: the oldest known wooden structure, built before Homo sapiens appears in the record.

name: Woven Cloth
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Preserved woven textile from Catalhoyuk — spinning and weaving, as distinct from the far older twisting of fibre into cord.

name: Writing
under: Behavioural Firsts < Human Prehistory < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Proto-cuneiform at Uruk and hieroglyphic tags at Abydos — two independent inventions whose dates overlap.

name: Denisovans
summary: A human population known mainly from DNA, identified from fragments in a Siberian cave and traceable in living people.

name: Homo antecessor
summary: An early European human from a Spanish cave, about 800,000 years old, whose status as a separate species is still argued.

name: Homo erectus
summary: The first widely travelled human species, present from about 1.9 million years ago until roughly 110,000 years ago in Java.

name: Homo floresiensis
summary: A small-bodied human on the Indonesian island of Flores, known from Liang Bua cave.

name: Homo habilis
summary: An early, small-brained human in Africa from about 2.4 to 1.4 million years ago, overlapping with other human species.

name: Homo heidelbergensis
summary: A large-brained Middle Pleistocene human in Europe, Africa and the Near East, roughly 700,000 to 200,000 years ago.

name: Homo longi
summary: A single large skull from Harbin, China, whose identity was overturned by protein analysis in 2025.

name: Homo luzonensis
summary: A human species known from a handful of bones and teeth in a cave on Luzon, the Philippines.

name: Homo naledi
summary: A small-brained human found deep in a South African cave system, surprisingly recent at 335,000 to 236,000 years ago.

name: Homo neanderthalensis
summary: Cold-adapted humans across Europe and western Asia, from about 400,000 years ago until roughly 40,000 years ago.

name: Homo rudolfensis
summary: A flat-faced, big-toothed early human from Kenya about 1.9 million years ago whose place in the human genus is still argued over.

name: Homo sapiens
summary: Our own species, first recognisable in Africa around 300,000 years ago.

name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
under: Cold War < Short 20th Century < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Symbolic end of the Cold War division of Europe; East Germans crossed freely on 9 November 1989.

name: Cuban Missile Crisis
under: Cold War < Short 20th Century < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Thirteen-day nuclear standoff between the US and USSR over Soviet missiles in Cuba — the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.

name: Korean War
under: Cold War < Short 20th Century < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: First major hot conflict of the Cold War; UN-backed South Korea vs. Chinese/Soviet-backed North.

name: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
under: Cold War < Short 20th Century < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon (20 July 1969).

name: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
under: Cold War < Short 20th Century < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Formal end of the USSR on 26 December 1991; 15 successor republics.

name: Vietnam War
under: Cold War < Short 20th Century < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Prolonged conflict ending with North Vietnamese victory and reunification.

name: World War I
summary: World War I — the first industrialized total war; ended four empires.

name: World War II
summary: World War II — the deadliest conflict in human history; ended with the atomic bombings of Japan.

name: Buddhism
summary: Began as a teaching about the causes of suffering and became the first tradition to spread across Asia by persuasion.

name: Christianity
summary: Began as a movement within Judaism and became the state religion of the empire that had executed its founder.

name: Confucianism
summary: A tradition about conduct, family and government rather than gods, and the framework of Chinese administration for two millennia.

name: Daoism
summary: Philosophy and later religion built on acting with the grain of things rather than against it.

name: The Great Schism
summary: Formal separation of the Latin and Greek churches, after centuries of drift over authority and doctrine.

name: Hinduism
summary: Less a single founding than a continuity of Vedic ritual, Upanishadic philosophy and devotional practice.

name: Islam
summary: Began at Mecca and Medina and within a century governed from Iberia to the Indus.

name: Jainism
summary: Holds non-violence as the first principle, extended to every living thing.

name: Judaism
summary: Took its lasting shape around exile and return, and around a text rather than a temple.

name: Mahayana Buddhism
summary: Shifted the goal from personal liberation to universal awakening, and carried Buddhism to China, Korea and Japan.

name: Manichaeism
summary: A deliberately universal religion that reached from Rome to China and then was extinguished almost everywhere.

name: Shinto
summary: Japanese practice centred on kami and place, defined as a distinct religion largely in response to Buddhism.

name: Sikhism
summary: Founded by Nanak in Punjab, rejecting caste and ritual in favour of one God and honest work.

name: Sufism
summary: The mystical current of Islam, and the form in which it most often spread through South Asia and West Africa.

name: The Sunni-Shia Split
summary: A dispute over succession to Muhammad that hardened into the enduring division of the Muslim world.

name: Theravada Buddhism
summary: The school that kept the Pali canon, dominant across Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia.

name: Vajrayana Buddhism
under: Mahayana Buddhism < Buddhism < Religions & Traditions < Global & Multi-Regional
summary: Tantric Buddhism, transmitted into Tibet and the Himalaya.

name: Zoroastrianism
summary: Persian tradition whose ideas about judgement, a final reckoning and cosmic dualism reached Judaism, Christianity and Islam.

name: Aboriginal Australians
summary: The longest continuous cultural tradition known, with oral accounts that appear to record post-glacial sea-level rise.

name: Arrival of the Dingo
summary: A dog carried to Australia by sea, and the clearest evidence of outside contact before Europeans.

name: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
summary: British troops opened fire on unarmed civilians in Amritsar; a decisive turning point in Indian nationalism.

name: Partition of India
summary: Division of British India into India and Pakistan; one of history's largest forced migrations, with mass violence.

name: Salt March / Salt Satyagraha
summary: Gandhi's 240-mile march to defy the British salt monopoly; galvanized mass civil disobedience.

name: Indian Rebellion of 1857
under: East India Company Rule < South Asia
summary: Massive uprising against Company rule; suppressed with great violence. Led directly to the establishment of the British Raj.

name: Bangladesh Liberation War
summary: East Pakistan's independence war; India intervened decisively. Birth of Bangladesh.

name: Sri Lankan Civil War
summary: Long conflict between the Sri Lankan government and the LTTE (Tamil Tigers); ended with the military defeat of the LTTE.

name: The Rakhigarhi Genome
summary: A single woman's DNA, recovered after 61 attempts, showed the Harappans carried no steppe ancestry and no Anatolian farmer ancestry.

name: Pottery Reaches Island Southeast Asia
under: The Austronesian Expansion < Southeast Asian Prehistory < Southeast Asia
summary: Pottery appears in Borneo and the northern Philippines at the same time, not one after the other.

name: Neolithic Migration into Southeast Asia
summary: East Asian farming populations move south and mix with resident Hoabinhian-descended foragers rather than replacing them.

name: Battle of Kadesh
summary: Hittites and Egyptians fight the best-documented battle of the Bronze Age to a stalemate, then sign a treaty a copy of which hangs at the UN.

name: Mursili I Sacks Babylon
summary: A Hittite raid ends Hammurabi's dynasty, and the date it happened is the hinge the whole Bronze Age chronology turns on.

name: The Invention of Coinage
summary: Struck electrum pieces of guaranteed weight appear in Lydia, and money stops having to be weighed out.

name: The Incense Route
summary: Frankincense and myrrh moving north out of South Arabia, the trade that paid for Saba, Qataban and eventually Petra.

name: Arab Conquest of Iran
summary: Eighteen years that ended the Sasanian empire and began the Islamic period in Iran.
